newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hanoi raises airfares for Vietnamese.
newsitem.headline: Hanoi raises airfares for Vietnamese.

text.p: Vietnam's national carrier, Vietnam Airlines, said on Wednesday fares for domestic passengers were being raised on all routes by 12.5 percent.
An official at the state-owned company said the new fares would be introduced on December 5.

The new fares mean that a Vietnamese national travelling on the country's busiest route between Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City will now have to pay 900,000 dong ($81) for a one-way economy class ticket instead of the 800,000 dong ($72) previously.
The price for foreigners remains unchanged at $170 for the same trip.
The rise is the second this year and is seen as a move to reintroduce an increase of up to 30 percent which was introduced and then cancelled by the government in 1995.
Fares were increased in April by 14.3 percent on the Hanoi to Ho Chi Minh City route.
Both increases have been approved by the government's pricing department.
